rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design should be the most reliable one the evidence supports. Iteration 8 (y 0.065, sensor_size 0.016, span x -0.07 to 0.07, base_speed 1.2, kp 2.6, ki 0.1, kd 0.6) is the best raced design at 431.06. Its oval was 20/20 finishes at mean 944 with max_error 0.033. Iteration 10 changed kd to 0.5 at the same geometry and scored 427.56. Its oval stayed 20/20 with a similar mean, but its s-bend and slalom were no better. The Evaluator's approved candidate is that kd 0.5 test, but it has already been raced and it lost 3.5 points, so re-racing it would add no information. Iteration 9 showed that lowering base_speed to 1.1 also does not clear the s-bend. Neither the s-bend nor the slalom has ever finished in any iteration, so the remaining gains sit on unseen-track robustness rather than dev-track tuning. I therefore return to the iteration 8 design unchanged: the oval is at its ceiling, its line-loss and oscillation are the lowest among the designs that held 20/20 on the oval, and it carries no unraced change into the final scored run. Expected result: about 431 on the development tracks, with the oval finishing 20/20. Measurements to read: completion, progress and max_error on each track, to see whether the s-bend and slalom still go off track at about 0.062 max_error, and line_loss_events, to check that y 0.065 does not lose the line on an unseen shape.
